title: Use Probability to Resist Overconfidence
coreMove: Anchor a forecast in base rates and margin of safety before vivid case evidence inflates confidence.
sourcePressure: The source highlights overestimated control, overestimated desired outcomes, neglected prior probability, ignored base rates, overweighted individual case evidence, coincidence, misleading patterns, margin of safety, and failure through many paths.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is telling people to be less confident. The chapter should make the reader change the order of thinking: base rate first, vivid case second, margin of safety before commitment.

hook: The numbers do not care how you feel
counterintuition: The unlikely event cannot happen twice

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: wildfire insurance underwriting for cabins near a newly thinned forest edge
exampleSpecs.audience: Emily, an underwriter tempted by fresh mitigation photos
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one neat property file overrides regional burn frequencies in the premium decision
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily writes the county burn base rate at the top of the file before opening the glossy mitigation photos
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the faint smoke smell in a courier envelope of cabin photos

exampleSpecs.domain: minor-league basketball scouting after one 38-point game
exampleSpecs.audience: Henrik, a scout whose coach wants to sign the player by Monday
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a single hot night beats three seasons of ordinary shooting percentages
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik covers the player's name, asks the room to predict next-season shooting from the three-year line, then reveals the highlight game last
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 10:12 p.m., Henrik pauses the highlight reel on a corner three

exampleSpecs.domain: medical clinic interpreting a positive screening result for a rare condition
exampleSpecs.audience: Sofia, a physician assistant explaining why the scary test is not a diagnosis yet
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a patient leaves panicked because case evidence outran prior probability
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sofia draws 1,000 small boxes on the exam-table paper and shades the base-rate group before discussing the positive result
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Before we talk about your result, I want to draw the whole room," beside crinkled exam paper

exampleSpecs.domain: product team reading an A/B test that barely cleared significance during a holiday spike
exampleSpecs.audience: Devon, a growth lead who wants to ship the winning button color
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether coincidence and seasonal traffic masquerade as a durable product improvement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Devon reruns the test excluding the holiday campaign traffic before letting the green lift number into the launch deck
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dashboard tile glowing green under a calendar full of holiday campaign blocks

exampleSpecs.domain: avalanche guide deciding whether blue sky overrides the snowpack bulletin
exampleSpecs.audience: Thomas, a backcountry guide with clients staring at perfect morning light
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether visible calm erases low-frequency but lethal risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas reads the persistent weak-layer bulletin aloud, sets a turnaround line on the map, and cuts the route despite the clear sky
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can hear ski skins rip in the blue morning while the bulletin sits in Thomas's glove

exampleSpecs.domain: museum curator authenticating a painting after one exciting provenance letter
exampleSpecs.audience: Kasia, a curator whose donor wants the find announced at the gala
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one vivid artifact beats the prior odds of a real lost masterwork
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia tapes the known forgery-rate estimate beside the provenance letter and delays the gala announcement until pigment testing returns
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cream-colored provenance letter under the cold lamp of a conservation table

skillTargets: apply base rates before case evidence
recognize coincidence in apparently meaningful clusters
choose a margin of safety under known unknowns
separate desired probability from actual probability

tryThisNowSpec: For one forecast you care about, write the base rate first, then the case detail that tempts you to ignore it, then one margin of safety.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
